test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 19 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is the nodal organisation for International Big Cat Alliance in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Tiger Conservation Authority**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)** is the nodal agency in India responsible for the implementation of the **International Big Cat Alliance**, which aims to conserve big cats globally. 
• The NTCA was established in **2005** under the provisions of the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, and is tasked with strengthening tiger conservation efforts in the country. 
• India launched the **International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA)** in **April 2023** at Mysuru, Karnataka, during the 50th anniversary celebrations of Project Tiger. It focuses on conserving seven species of big cats: Tigers, Lions, Leopards, Snow Leopards, Cheetahs, Jaguars, and Pumas. 
• The alliance is open to **97 range countries** that are home to big cats and aims to facilitate collaboration, research, and funding for conservation initiatives. 
• The NTCA oversees the implementation of various conservation measures, including **habitat restoration, anti-poaching operations, and wildlife monitoring**, and works in coordination with international organizations for big cat protection. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):** 
• The NTCA is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change. It was constituted as part of **Project Tiger**, which was launched in **1973** to protect India's tiger population. 
• It formulates policies for tiger conservation, monitors implementation, and provides funding for tiger reserves across India. 
• As of 2023, India has **53 tiger reserves**, covering approximately **75,000 sq km** of protected area. 
• The NTCA also collaborates with international agencies such as the **Global Tiger Forum** to strengthen conservation efforts. 
• **Project Tiger:** 
• Launched in **1973**, Project Tiger is one of India's most significant wildlife conservation programs, aiming to protect tigers and their habitats. 
• The project seeks to reduce human-wildlife conflict, restore ecosystems, and prevent poaching. 
• India is home to approximately **70% of the global tiger population**, making it a leader in tiger conservation. 
• According to the latest census in **2022**, India’s tiger population stands at **3,167**. 
• **International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA):** 
• The IBCA was launched in **2023** to promote global collaboration in conserving big cats like tigers, lions, snow leopards, and cheetahs. 
• The initiative is guided by India's successful tiger conservation model under Project Tiger. 
• It focuses on research, habitat management, community engagement, and funding conservation efforts across range countries. 
• India has committed to supporting the alliance financially for the first five years, with a funding of **$100 million**. 
• **Other Relevant Organizations:** 
• **Wildlife Institute of India (WII):** It provides research and training to support wildlife conservation, including tiger monitoring initiatives. 
• **Central Wildlife Control Board:** Focuses on addressing wildlife-related issues and supports anti-poaching efforts but does not directly oversee big cat conservation. 
• **National Lion Protection Authority:** While lions are part of big cat conservation, this specific entity is not tasked with international alliances like the IBCA. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **India's Leadership in Big Cat Conservation:** 
• India's successful tiger conservation under Project Tiger has become a model for other countries globally. 
• India reintroduced **cheetahs** from Namibia and South Africa under the **Cheetah Reintroduction Program** in **2022**. 
• India plays a pivotal role in fostering international collaboration for big cat conservation through initiatives like IBCA. 
• **Global Tiger Day:** 
• Celebrated annually on **29th July** to raise awareness about tiger conservation worldwide. 
• The day highlights the importance of protecting tiger habitats and combating threats like deforestation and poaching.
